recipes.name: Peanut Butter and Banana Dog Biscuits
ingredients_raw: 1 egg white, lightly beaten, for brushing

steps.text: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.

Stir together the egg, peanut butter, banana, and honey in a medium bowl; blend thoroughly. Stir in the flour and wheat germ; mix well. Turn dough out onto a floured board and roll to 1/4 inch thick. Cut into desired shapes with a cookie cutter, place on prepared baking sheet, and brush tops with egg white.
Bake biscuits in preheated oven until dried and golden brown, about 30 minutes, depending on size. Remove from oven and cool on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter and Banana Dog Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: Crisp and crunchy, these easy-to-make, rolled, cut-out dog cookies combine peanut butter, honey, and an egg with whole wheat flour and wheat germ.

video.description: Give your dog a bone! Your dog is sure to love these biscuits, made with peanut butter, banana, and honey.

review.reviewBody: I followed the recipe as close as I could with what I had on hand. Instead of wheat germ I used wheat bran, which is naturally 'sweet'. Since my Labrador needs no additional reason to be happy I also left out the honey. Out of the 2 dog biscuit recipes I have he prefers this one, it's more peanutty. (I know I tried a bite). It only made 14 biscuits with a medium-size round biscuit cutter, so next time I will at least double the recipe. As for the cook - don't be stingy with the flour when rolling it out. thank you!

Girls love these, I used oatmeal instead of flour and graham crumbs( time to clean out the cupboards). As we use these for training treats rather than use a cookie cutter I roll the dough out on parchment paper and cut it into half inch squares using a pizza cutter, place on a cookie sheet and you are done, fast and easy

This dough was surprisingly easy to work with right out of the bowl! I sub'd the honey with one T of Sugar free Blackberry jam (Smuckers),& rolled oats for the wheat germ. I then refrigerated it overnight, & it didn't stick at all! I rolled it right on my silicone cutting board with a silicone roller. I cut some with mini cookie cutters & some I just shaped into rounds with my hands. Never stuck to anything! The finished product came out super! Crisp & pretty! I did have to cook them longer to get extra crisp, but well worth it. Doggies can't get enough!!

This recipe is Scotty dog approved. I also took it to Christmas with the family, and the puppy cousins also loved these cookies! I used oatmeal instead of wheat germ, and did not roll the dough out but did drop cookies and flattened them with my fingers. I will be making these quite often for my dog.

For Christmas, I received a dog biscuit mold, and used it to make biscuits today. I rolled about a tablespoon into a little log and squished it into the mold...much easier than rolling and cutting. See my attached picture.

These were instantly snapped up! I made them for a dog obedience training school open house. I increased the peanut butter to 1/2 cup and subbed flax meal for the wheat germ. I also used ripe bananas that I had previously frozen, so was glad to find another use for them. The dough was a perfect consistency to roll out.

These are amazing and my dogs love them, I substituted wheat flour for coconut flour, completely left out the wheat germ, and used 1/4 of a cup of applesauce. Baked for 25 mins and they turn out perfect !
I doubled the recipe, except for the honey. Kept the honey as 1 T and also used oats instead of wheat germ. My dog loved them!

My dog is a senior, so I used 1/2 c. gluten free and 1/2 c. shredded unsweetened coconut, 2T. ground flax, eliminated the honey and 1 egg. It was a little dry, so I added a small amount of water. After 30 min. of baking I turned the oven off and let them for an hour. They are crunchy and my dog love them!

I used what I had on hand: regular unbleached flour and regular oatmeal (instead of the wheat germ).
I did not brush the tops with egg white (the dogs don't care if it's shiny!).
I used a whole banana rather than measuring a 1/2 cup.
I added extra flour before trying to roll it out because it was too sticky. (probably from the extra banana).
I used a pizza cutter to cut diamond shapes (long cuts one way, long cuts the other way).
I didn't grease the baking sheet (it's an old non-stick sheet).

I'll definitely make these again. The dogs like them, it's a simple recipe, and I know what the ingredients are.

I ran out of Dog treats this weekend and didn't want to make a trip into town. B-i-n-g-o! I found this yummy recipe I could make from what I already had in my cabinets. 

I substituted rolled oats for the wheat germ and water for the honey - all the same amounts. Twenty minutes in the oven, and B-i-n-g-o! All Recipes saved the day and made my Bella one happy pup! 

I saved myself a little time by rolling into balls with my hands and using a fork to press the dough like miniature peanut butter cookies because essentially, this is what they are! My Bella loved them! I'm already making batch number two! I would recommend doubling the recipe, especially if you have more than one dog! 

I took some photos, but this is my first time here. If I can find a way to upload... I'll share! Another day I'd like to try using some of my frozen blueberries in them. You could also use a little applesauce! Thank you! These are GREAT!

My dogs love these cookies. I've made them as written, but also made them gluten free using ground golden flax seeds, chickpea flour and almond meal and they turned out great. I use a small ice cream scoop and place the balls on a cookie sheet and freeze the dough balls. I cut each ball of dough in four pieces before baking as to make nice small cookies, good for training.

Used as a baseline with the ingredients I had on hand. I used all purpose flour and canned yams in place of the banana. I also shortened the baking time to keep them a bit on the soft side for my oldest master. Yummy... yes I tried one. :) *Finally used my Pampered Chef small cookie cutters since my babies are on the small side.

my dogs love these . I quadrupled the recipe, and added xtra honey, as my dogs have enviromental allergies, and strange as it seems, giving them honey helps cut down the allergy to pollen. I also added in plain yogurt. they love them!
Great cookies, my dog and even my kid liked them :D I just had to add 1 tablespoon of water to the dough to make it smoother and easier to roll out.
I used a quarter cup of applesauce in place of the egg and ground up my oats for the wheat germ. Dog loves them.

OMG ! First time making dog treats. My dogs love them. My Bull Mastiff I made her bigger but my other dogs they were waiting around for them because they smelled the peanut butter! Will triple the recipe So I don’t have to make them, but once a week

My puppy waited somewhat patiently as my kitchen smelled like a big peanut butter treat! After baking, she woofed them down for tricks and would’ve eaten every single one if I let her! I told her we were sharing with her neighborhood doggy friend.
Recipe is great and they taste good. The only problem is my fussy Cavapoo doesn’t like them so guess I’ll be eating them!
I used oats instead of wheat germ as others suggested. Our Pom loves them!
